title: KV-prefetch audit and experiment guide
author: Maya R. Singh
body:
Overview
This document is a pragmatic audit + experiment playbook for evaluating and iterating on KV-cache prefetch strategies in the Redwood serving runtime. It consolidates instrumentation, test-corpus design, hypothesis-driven experiments, safety gates, and clear remediation steps to validate that a prefetch change improves throughput or cost without regressing latency or output fidelity.

Intended audience
- Runtime engineers (kernel and scheduler owners)
- Performance and profiling teams
- SREs running capacity and incident drills
- Release engineers validating runtime rollouts

Goals
1) Provide a repeatable audit checklist to assess existing prefetch behaviour and its observability gaps.
2) Define experiment templates (canary, A/B, ramp) with required telemetry, sample sizes, and SLO-aligned success criteria.
3) Offer rollout and rollback runbook steps with specific threshold values and playbook actions.

Scope and non-goals
- Scope: KV prefetch heuristics, warmup policies, prefetch batch sizing, prefetch prioritisation across tenants/model variants, and their impact on kernel scheduling and KV cache hit/miss behavior.
- Non-goals: Changes to model serialization or offline model compile pipeline (handled elsewhere). This guide does not substitute for security or compliance sign-off for customer-sensitive telemetry.

Background and terminology
- KV prefetch: pro-active population of a model's key-value cache before predicted use (e.g., during warmstart or after canary shadowing).
- Warmstart: placement of a model variant onto a GPU with pre-warmed KV state for a target user session.
- Prefetch window: sequence-length- and token-count-derived horizon for which we request early KV population.
- Shadow traffic: mirrored request streams used for dry-run experiments.

Observability contract (what to collect)
Collect these signals for all experiments. Instrumentation must be enabled at service, runtime-shard, and kernel levels.
- Metrics (per-second or histogram as noted):
  - kvcache.prefetch.requests_total (counter)
  - kvcache.prefetch.success_ratio (gauge) = success / attempts per minute
  - kvcache.hit_ratio_by_prefix_length (histogram buckets by prefix tokens)
  - kvcache.prefetch_latency_p50/p95 (histogram ms)
  - kernel.queue_wait_ms (histogram) labeled by priority bucket
  - runtime.topology.eviction_rate (counter per shard)
  - gpu.memory.oversubscription_events (counter)
  - request.latency.p50/p95/p99 (end-to-end including network + kernel)
  - request.tail_slo_breaches (counter) where tail SLO := requests > configured target (e.g., 95th > 120ms)
  - cost.per_token.estimated (derived using token counts + kernel accounting)
- Traces: request span with children: prefetch.call, prefetch.cache_write, kernel.exec, kv_lookup; include tags: model_id, variant_tag, session_id, shard_id, kernel_id, tenant_id, prefetch_hint_id.
- Logs: structured event for prefetch decisions: {"decision":"prefetch|skip","reason":"prefix-match|heuristic|manual","estimated_tokens":N,"evicted":true|false,"latency_ms":N} as newline-delimited JSON to the observability pipeline.

Audit checklist (baseline assessment)
1) Baseline traffic capture
   - Capture at least 72 hours of representative production traffic or use a validated synthetic corpus (see Test corpus section).
   - Ensure sampling includes peak hour and low-hour slices.
2) Reproduceability of prefetch events
   - Verify prefetch events are traceable to requests in shadow logs. Correlate prefetch_hint_id across traces.
3) Telemetry completeness
   - Confirm all metrics and traces listed in Observability contract are present. If any are missing, add target instrumentation and replay a synthetic subset to validate.
4) Heatmaps and correlation checks
   - Build the following diagnostics:
     - heatmap: prefix_length -> prefetch_success_rate
     - scatter: per-request prefetch_latency vs request_latency
     - timeline: eviction_rate vs memory_pressure
5) Failure mode inventory
   - Enumerate cases found in logs (e.g., prefetch eviction within 2s, prefetch causing kernel queueing). Classify severity and likely root causes.

Test corpus recommendations
- Canonical corpora: use a mix of (a) production-scrubbed request traces, (b) replayable synthetic sessions (session bundles), and (c) jittered-edge sequences to exercise long prefixes.
- Session bundle format (JSONL, one session per line):
  {"session_id":"s-123","model":"vicuna-13b-q4","turns":["Hello","Summarize: ...","Followup: ..."],"timestamps":[...]}
- Size guidance: minimum 5000 sessions covering 10k prefix variations for a statistically meaningful p95 comparison in canary windows.

Experiment designs
All experiments must be hypothesis-driven and limited in blast radius. Follow the experiment checklist below.

A) Shadow (no impact) hypothesis test
- Goal: Validate prefetch hit-rate and false-positive eviction costs without affecting production latency.
- Method: Mirror 1:1 traffic to a shadow runtime with the new prefetch strategy. Do not route responses.
- Duration: 48–72 hours or until 10k prefetch decisions observed.
- Required metrics: kvcache.prefetch.success_ratio, eviction_rate, prefetch_latency.
- Success criteria: improvement in prefetch.success_ratio by >=5% or reduction in cold-start kernel execs by >=10% with no increase in eviction_rate > 2% over baseline.

B) Canary small ramp (impactful but controlled)
- Goal: Measure end-to-end latency and kernel queue impact under production conditions.
- Method: Route 1% of traffic to canary pool with the new prefetch strategy. Use canary tags and separate metrics.
- Observation windows: 1 minute, 15 minutes, 1 hour, 6 hours.
- Safety gates (auto-rollback triggers):
  - request.tail_slo_breaches increases by >20% relative to baseline in a 15-minute window -> immediate rollback.
  - kernel.queue_wait_ms.p95 increases by >30% sustained for 10 minutes -> immediate pause and manual review.
  - gpu.memory.oversubscription_events > 0 (new events) in canary -> pause.
- Success criteria: no SLO breach increase; p95 request latency change within +/- 5% and prefetch.success_ratio improved or neutral.

C) A/B experiment with fidelity measurement
- Goal: Measure fidelity / model output drift when prefetching influences KV state timing (rare but possible).
- Method: 50/50 split where identical prompts are sent to control (no change) and candidate (new prefetch). Collect deterministic evaluation prompts and human-eval random sample.
- Fidelity metrics: BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity on deterministic prompts, plus small human quality cohort (n=200) to detect hallucination/regression.
- Success criteria: embedding cosine similarity > 0.995 on deterministic prompts and no statistically significant decrease in human-score (alpha=0.05).

Telemetry and sample size calculations
- Latency experiments: to detect a 5% p95 change with 90% power typically needs O(20k) p95 samples per group; for canaries prefer longer duration instead of increasing blast radius.
- Hit-rate experiments: to detect a 5% absolute increase in hit rate with alpha=0.05/power=0.8, ~thousands of prefetch events are required depending on baseline rate; use exact binomial test calculator.

Experiment orchestration and dashboards
- Dashboards: create canary-specific dashboards with the prefixed label canary=kv-prefetch-vX. Panels: prefetch.success_ratio, request.p95, kernel.queue_wait_ms.p95, eviction_rate, memory_pressure, tail_slo_breaches; include shaded baseline band.
- Alerts: temporary canary alerts that auto-resolve after ramp is complete.

Rollout and rollback runbook (step-by-step)
1) Preflight (1–3 days before canary)
   - Verify instrumentation and dashboards are green.
   - Run shadow test and ensure metrics are recorded.
   - Prepare rollback image and clear owner contact list.
2) Canary 1% (0–2 hours)
   - Deploy config to canary pool. Monitor 1m and 15m windows.
   - If any auto-rollback trigger fires, execute rollback playbook (step 5).
3) Ramp to 5% (2–12 hours)
   - After 6 hours of stable signals, increment to 5%. Continue monitoring 1m/15m/1h/6h windows.
4) Ramp to 20% (12–48 hours)
   - Confirm A/B fidelity checks pass on deterministic prompts.
5) Full roll (48–72 hours)
   - Only after 72 hours with no gate violations and cost analysis favorable, schedule full rollout.
6) Rollback procedure (when triggered)
   - Step A: Pause canary routing (set weight=0).
   - Step B: Revert runtime config to previous prefetch policy image.
   - Step C: Collect postmortem trace dump, capture 2-hour window around trigger for RCA.
   - Step D: Open incident with severity classification and tag owners.

Common failure modes and mitigations
- Failure: Increased kernel queueing due to premature prefetch floods.
  - Mitigation: Add rate limiter on prefetch.requests per shard per second; add backpressure signal from kernel.queue_wait_ms.
- Failure: Prefetch evicts hot state for other tenants.
  - Mitigation: Implement tenant-aware prefetch budgeting and soft reservations.
- Failure: Memory oversubscription from prefetch writes.
  - Mitigation: Pre-allocate lightweight shadow stores and throttle writes when memory_pressure > 70%.

Debugging checklist (fast triage)
1) Correlate prefetch decision trace with kernel.exec and eviction events (trace id).
2) If prefetch_latency_p95 > 100ms, inspect network path and serialization overhead.
3) If eviction_rate spikes after prefetch, check memory per shard, recent model swaps, and estimate of prefetch window size.
4) Re-run small synthetic session set in debug pool with verbose logging on canary image.

Example config snippets
- Prefetch policy YAML (example):
```yaml
prefetch_policy: 
  name: horizon-predictor-v2
  enabled: true
  max_concurrent_per_shard: 8
  token_horizon: 64
  priority: low
  tenant_budget_percent: 5
  eviction_backoff_seconds: 30
  metrics_emit_interval_s: 10
```
- CLI commands (examples)
  - Capture shadow stream (devbox):
    rdxctl kvcapture --model vicuna-13b-q4 --window 72h --out /tmp/vicuna-shadow.jsonl
  - Deploy canary config:
    rdxctl deploy-config --pool canary-kv-prefetch-v2 --config ./prefetch-policy.yaml --tag kv-prefetch-v2
  - Pause canary routing:
    rdxctl set-weight --pool canary-kv-prefetch-v2 --weight 0

Post-experiment analysis and documentation checklist
- Produce a short experiment report that includes: hypothesis, traffic windows used, sample sizes, raw metrics time-series, heatmaps, global and per-tenant impact, cost delta estimate, and recommended next action (rollback, tweak, full rollout).
- Archive experiment artifacts: traces, dashboards, config version, and sample sessions used for reproducibility.
- If fidelity regressions observed, escalate to model onboarding and research for root-cause and mitigation.

Ownership and escalation
- Primary owner: Runtime performance team (runtime-perf@redwood.com).
- Secondary owner: SRE (sre-runtime@redwood.com).
- Pager: oncall-runtime (pager duty) for canary auto-rollback events.

Appendix A — example dashboards (text sketch)
- Row 1: Prefetch overview: success_ratio (time-series), requests_total (time-series)
- Row 2: Kernel impact: kernel.queue_wait_ms.p95 (compare canary/control), kernel.exec_count_per_min
- Row 3: Memory & eviction: runtime.topology.eviction_rate, gpu.memory.oversubscription_events
- Row 4: Fidelity: embedding_similarity distribution between control/canary for deterministic prompts

Appendix B — experiment templates (copyable)
- Shadow runbook checklist (copyable):
  1. Confirm instrumentation (metrics + trace tags).
  2. Start shadow capture for N=72h.
  3. Run offline analyser: rdx-analyse-shadow --input /tmp/vicuna-shadow.jsonl --report /tmp/prefetch-shadow-report.html
  4. Review heatmaps and fill Failure mode inventory table.
